correctness.rationale: The explicit hub/rim NOR rule has a complete, disjoint three-case basin preimage classification. The exact identity g²(x)_i=x_i OR (x_{i-2} AND x_{i+2}) and g³=g rules out later zero-rim surprises. Every state reaches recurrence within one step and the boundary n=3,4 is included. Cyclic distance-two constraints have one or two disjoint components as appropriate; trace([[0,1],[1,1]]^m)=L_m counts their valid words. Two independent included checkers pass over 11 full state spaces and independent transfer tests. Finite checks are ancillary to the all-n proof.

value.rationale: A wheel is the canonical single-hub perturbation of a cycle. The bare-cycle empty/full oscillator attracts T_n+1 states, a probability tending to zero, whereas the wheel version attracts 2^n+T_n, a probability tending to one-half. The observable is the exact selection probability of a naturally distinguished oscillator, not an arbitrary parameter or a finite slice. The proof establishes >50% dominance for all sizes, exponential approach to half, and an exact mod-four correction reflecting the two parity subcycles of the rim total-domination constraint. This gives a reusable benchmark for basin concentration in inhibitory Boolean networks without requiring a census of other attractors.
